---
title: "Unemployment in one region"
subtitle: "Synthetic data, for training only"
date: today
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
execute:
  echo: false
---


```{r}
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(tinytable)
rates <- readr::read_csv("unemployment.csv")
REGION <- "Tabuk"
area    <- subset(rates, region == REGION)
kingdom <- subset(rates, region == "Kingdom")
now  <- tail(area$rate, 1)
then <- head(area$rate, 1)
gap  <- now - tail(kingdom$rate, 1)
```

## Summary

In `r REGION` the rate was `r sprintf("%.1f", now)`% in 2025 Q4,
`r sprintf("%+.1f", now - then)` points since 2022 Q1 and
`r sprintf("%+.1f", gap)` points against the Kingdom
(@fig-trend, @fig-compare, @tbl-recent).

## Trend

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Unemployment rate,", REGION, "(%)")
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
ggplot(area, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-compare
#| fig-cap: "Against the Kingdom"
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-subcap: ["Both series", "The last four quarters"]
both <- subset(rates, region %in% c(REGION, "Kingdom"))
ggplot(both, aes(date, rate, colour = region)) +
  geom_line()
last4 <- subset(both, quarter >= "2025Q1")
ggplot(last4, aes(quarter, rate, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")
```

## Latest quarters

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recent
#| tbl-cap: !expr paste("Unemployment rate,", REGION, "(%)")
tt(tail(area[, c("quarter", "rate")], 4)) |>
  theme_html(portable = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Method"}
Rates are the unemployed as a share of the labour force.
The data are synthetic, made for training.
:::
